searchText: Out of curiosity when do you guys think fees will become lowered, is sharding what will fix fees or is there a different phase that will lower them down the line. Just wondering Also I hope someone who truly understands ETH 2.0 development threads can clarify my confusion. From my understanding, ETH 2.0 will introduce POS with all the scalability benefits vs POW. My understanding is that ETH 2.0 will implement Friendly Finality Gadget (FFG) not Correct By Construction (CBC). To call FFG a POS distributed consensus algorithm is stretching the truth and therefore over exaggerating ETH 2.0 scalability benefits (without Layer 2 that could be used with ETH 1.0 POW anyway). FFG is at the core POW with POS overlayed to achieve finality in epochs. It wont achieve any scalability because at it's core it is POW. CBC is true POS as implemented by the renegade Casper network. Isn't ETH 2.0 on this basis just propaganda and the whole Beacon/FFG thread is a waste of time. Please help my confusion. Eip 1011 (hybrid pow/pos using ffg dor finality) was deprecated in 2018 EIP 3675 describes how the beacon chain (who's consensus is driven by ffg) will become the new pure pos consensus for ethereum mainnet PoS itself does not scale a blockchain But you can create a sharded blockchain easier with pos and pow to add scale So, using that "safe-merge" approach, it might be possible to make multiple "merge" tests on mainnet before performing actual merge. Or am I wrong? <dankrad> you can do these tests anyway without doing the "safe merge". <dankrad> Safe merge is in fact a very unsafe idea Right, we can run the Merge testnets with the mainnet data and we will likely do this. But the idea of such testnets isn't related to the Safe Merge idea In The Safe Merge approach _multiple "merge" tests_ are more valuable as this better replicates the mainnet conditions. _multiple "merge" tests_ in The Merge approach doesn't address the fact that once-in-a-lifetime The Merge approach is much more attractive for attackers than the attempt-until-success approach in The Safe Merge. One of the main motivations of The Safe Merge is to address the unknown factors (i.e. attacks that we do not know even exist), but feel free to read the full discussion, there are pros and cons as always. <dankrad> I think it's a great idea to run merge on mainnet a few times. In fact one of the worries might be that some apps that need time-critical inputs (oracles, liquidations) are slow to upgrade and cause havoc. We should have some official tests where they can all test their infrastructure end-to-end (re @merge_chat_bot: <Mikhail Kalinin [mkalinin]> Right, we can run the Merge testnets with the mainnet data and we will likely do this. But the idea of such testnets isn't related to the Safe Merge idea) <ralexstokes> I think you mean to say run the merge process on a testnet *like mainnet* multiple times <ralexstokes> imo it will be disruptive to facilitate multiple actual merges on mainnet <dankrad> I would suggest using the actual mainnet data <dankrad> why would it be disruptive? <ralexstokes> sure but on testnets <dankrad> of course the resulting mergenets would be testnets <ralexstokes> im just clarifying “mainnet data” vs “doing the actual merge on mainnet" <dankrad> but I want people to be able to do 100% end to end testing on them <ralexstokes> yep sure

excerpts.content:
Eip 1011 (hybrid pow/pos using ffg dor finality) was deprecated in 2018

EIP 3675 describes how the beacon chain (who's consensus  is driven by ffg) will become the new pure pos consensus for ethereum mainnet
